meta.notes: First live run of method v1. Many vendor and review sites (letsbuild, sitemate, Capterra, TrustRadius, Software Advice, OpenSpace, Autodesk) block Preuve's crawler via robots.txt or HTTP 403, so they were left out rather than cited unverifiably. Two candidate job postings had expired. No first-hand practitioner time measurements for reporting were found in verifiable sources; vendor time claims (2-4 h per weekly report) were seen in search snippets only and are not included. Key contradiction: the incumbent Procore (46.2% PM adoption in the 2021 ConTech survey) markets AI agents that draft daily logs from field photos and summarize progress for stakeholders.

summary.statement: At one general contractor, the project engineer compiles and sends the weekly owner report each Friday and a manager reviews it before it is issued.
Report format and content vary by owner.
Many firms still share project data mainly by email, text and phone, and over half move data between unintegrated apps by hand.
Field capture (daily reports, photos) is already mostly done on mobile devices, so the remaining manual work is likely in compiling and formatting rather than capturing.
No verified first-hand account of a PM's end-to-end reporting workflow was found; this needs interviews.
Only a general figure was verified: 14+ hours per week of non-optimal time per team member, which does not isolate reporting.
Reporting-specific time figures seen during research came from vendor marketing and could not be verified; measure this in interviews.
Industry go-to-market guidance holds that PMs champion construction software while the CFO is the economic buyer.
Technology investment is framed as an executive decision.
Over a third of firms spend under 1% of sales on IT, so budgets for new tools may be tight.
Procore is the most-used project management software (46.2% of respondents in 2021).
Procore already markets AI agents that draft daily logs from field photos, notes and audio, and that summarize daily logs into stakeholder progress updates.
More than two-fifths of firms still use spreadsheets for project management.
AI progress capture from 360-degree site imagery (OpenSpace) is an established adjacent category.
Weekly owner reports are produced every Friday at at least one general contractor.
Monthly progress reports to owners and lenders are a standard contract and loan requirement, sometimes due within five days of month end.

hypothesis_update.problem: Compiling owner-facing weekly reports and monthly owner/lender progress reports from field data (photos, daily logs) is manual work spread across unintegrated tools, even where field capture is already digital.
hypothesis_update.users: Project engineers who draft the reports and project managers who review them, at US general contractors
hypothesis_update.buyer: Likely the CFO or financial executive (economic buyer), with PMs as internal champions
hypothesis_update.decision_maker: Likely the owner or an executive (final sign-off)
hypothesis_update.economic_value: Reduces time engineers and PMs spend compiling and formatting recurring owner and lender reports.

rationale.statement: The weekly report is drafted by the project engineer and reviewed by a manager, not written by the PM alone.
Monthly owner/lender progress reports are contractually required in addition to weekly ones.
Capture is largely digital already while data transfer between tools is manual, which moves the problem toward compiling rather than capturing.
Budget authority likely sits with the CFO, with PMs as champions.

new_unknowns.question: How well do Procore's AI daily log and progress-update agents work in practice, and what gaps remain for owner- and lender-facing reports?
Do general contractors that don't use Procore have a reporting workflow painful enough to adopt a standalone tool?
How long does a project engineer spend compiling one weekly owner report, and one monthly lender report?
